Remarks: At the commencement of the war was working in Tex., and not wishing to take up arms against his relatives in the North States. His home is in Massachusetts. On arriving at New Orleans, La., he was not permitted to go farther, being without friends or money, he was forced to join the Confed. Army. Enlisting in the 6th La. Inf., as a Pvt., he served in that capacity seven months, and was then promoted 2nd Lt. .ranking as such up to the time of his capture at Rappahannock Station, Va., Nov. 7, 1863. His object in wishing to take the Oath of Allegiance is to get out of prison, and leave the Confed. service forever. That he never owned any property in the South, does not sympathize with them at all. Occupation is that of laborer. Released on Oath of Allegiance to U. S., from Johnson's Island, Ohio, May 12. 1S65.
